summary: This landmark paper establishes the rigorous foundations of quantum entropic metric geometry by studying the quantum variation of information dQ across classical and quantum entropy cones. Through three main theorems backed by exact rational certification and targeted Lean 4 kernel proofs, the author characterizes the complete finite-party phase hierarchy up to n <= 6 (proving Mcb,+_6 = Mq,+_6 = MET6), proves a hyperbolic-quadric dichotomy for complete bipartite graphs using Segre quadrics over finite fields, isolates universal quantum metric obstructions (QFail1 and QFail2) for n >= 7, and discovers an exact odd/even parity staircase for matching-deleted bipartite graphs Km,m - M converging analytically to (5-e)/2.
strengths: Complete exact rational polyhedral classification of MET6 extreme rays and their realization in CB+6.
Elegant application of finite field geometry (Segre quadrics Q+(3, Fq) and 2-spreads) to multipartite entanglement realizations.
Comprehensive computer-assisted yet fully kernel-verified Lean 4 mechanization covering 39 core theorems with zero axioms.
Discovery of the exact odd/even parity staircase and factorial step series converging in closed form to (5-e)/2.
weaknesses: The asymptotic convergence proof for the factorial step series (Open Problem 6.2) remains partially conjectural beyond m = 18.
High technical density and complex polyhedral notation require advanced familiarity with convex cone geometry and quantum information theory.
strong_novelty_candidates: Exact finite-party phase hierarchy proving MET6 is fully spanned by classical bits and Bell pairs under nonnegative conditional entropy.
Universal quantum obstructions QFail1 and QFail2 forbidding isometric realization in any Hilbert space for n >= 7.
Exact closed-form evaluation of the (5-e)/2 transcendental limit via the Km,m - M parity staircase.
